title: OKF concept frontmatter
description: Validates the YAML frontmatter of every markdown concept, decision, meeting note and context file in this knowledge base. OKF core fields plus four documented local extensions. Absent `status` means stable.

type.description: What kind of record this is. Free-form, but these are the values in use.

title.description: Human-readable name. Not an OKF requirement; required here, and enforced rather than left to convention.

description.description: One or two sentences on what this concept covers.

resource.description: What this concept is *about* in the outside world, e.g. an Oracle object reference such as OMS_PROD.INVOICE_LINE, an ODI mapping name, or a URL.

tags.description: Free-form retrieval aids. Include vocabulary variants so grep finds this file under any of the terms people actually use.

status.description: Omit when the concept is stable — absent means stable. `draft` for an open question or a matter deferred with no decision yet. `accepted` for a decision that stands. `superseded` when a later record replaces this one; set `superseded_by` alongside it.

stale_after.description: ISO 8601 date after which this record should be re-checked against sources.

generated.description: Machine provenance. Required on every authored concept.

by.description: `<mode>:<agent>`, with `/<stage>` where the mode has stages. `process:claude-sonnet/variances` is a transform stage; `live-capture:claude-opus` is a live human capture, which has no stage. The pattern constrains shape only — it does not enumerate modes or agents, so a new mode, or an agent that is not Claude, needs no schema change.

at.description: RFC 3339 date-time, machine-stamped at write time. Date-time only — a bare date is not accepted, because the machine writing this always knows the time; the date a record refers to belongs in `updated`. Quote the value in YAML: an unquoted timestamp is auto-typed by PyYAML-based tooling and re-serialised space-separated, and this pattern is the tripwire for that round-trip.

verified.description: Human review record. NOT to be written by any transform stage — human review is recorded separately.

captured_by.description: LOCAL EXTENSION (not OKF). The human who brought this knowledge in — who took the call, sat in the room, or dictated the capture. Distinct from `generated.by`, which names the agent that wrote the file, and from the git author, who may be neither of them.

contested.description: LOCAL EXTENSION (not OKF). A dispute over one claim inside this file. Claim-level, not file-level: the record stays `accepted` while a single claim in it is contested. Not for a fact that was replaced by a later one (use `supersedes`/`superseded_by`), not for an open question where nobody asserts a competing value (use `status: draft`), and not for two statements of the same figure that differ only in rounding or precision.

claim.description: The field or claim in dispute, named in a few words.

positions.description: The competing positions, two or more.

source.description: Bundle-relative path to the artifact carrying this position. Omit when the position is not evidenced — never invent provenance.

held_by.description: Who or what holds this position — a person, or a named location inside a document where two parts of one artifact disagree. This is what separates the positions when both cite the same source file.

resolution_owner.description: Who is accountable for settling the dispute — not who holds one side of it. Required: write `none recorded` when nobody has been named, so an unowned dispute stays visible instead of being silently absent.

resolves_when.description: The future trigger that would settle this — the check, confirmation or decision that ends the dispute. Required: write `none recorded` when nothing has been identified.

sources.description: Provenance for the factual claims in this file. Every claim must trace to a /_sources/ artifact. Presence is required by tools/check_sources.py rather than by this schema, because the one legitimate exception is conditional on `type`: an `index` record is generated from the file tree and has no /_sources/ origin. minItems only fires when the key is present, so presence has to be checked somewhere.

id.description: Artifact ID from the manifest, e.g. DOC-03, EM-055, T-04.

last_modified.description: Date of the source artifact. Note: last_modified, NOT date.

owner.description: LOCAL EXTENSION (not OKF). Person accountable for the thing described, e.g. a variance owner.

updated.description: LOCAL EXTENSION (not OKF). Date this record last changed. Consulted when deciding which of two conflicting statements is current.

supersedes.description: LOCAL EXTENSION (not OKF). Bundle-relative path to the record this replaces.

superseded_by.description: LOCAL EXTENSION (not OKF). Bundle-relative path to the record that replaces this one. Set alongside status: superseded — never delete the old file.
